title: The feds are looking into reports of Tesla’s robotaxis speeding through school zones
key_facts: NHTSA, the US auto safety regulator, says it is evaluating allegations that Tesla's roughly 1,000 robotaxis using its automated driving system exceed posted speed limits in active school zones.

NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation received a defect petition on 23 Sep 2026 asking it to investigate model year 2026 Tesla Robotaxis (Model Y and Cybercab) with the automated driving system engaged.
The petitioner alleges the system exceeds posted speed limits in active school zones; the report does not name the petitioner.
The Cybercab launched earlier this year and is already under investigation over its lack of side mirrors, pedals and a steering wheel.
NHTSA has also opened an investigation into Tesla's Full Self-Driving system for traffic violations such as running red lights and driving on the wrong side of the street.
Waymo's robotaxis have faced similar inquiries, including for illegally passing school buses and hitting a child near a California elementary school.

why_it_matters_hint: About 1,000 driverless cars are alleged to speed where children cross; a regulator is evaluating the claim but has found nothing yet.
